grounding: The post (2026-11-23) says the Army hired Munirem, an explosives disposal company, to chemically disable degraded lead-based detonators but cancelled the contract and chose two-story sand barriers and a "water mist" instead; it links an Iowa Public Radio article and attaches a graphic of a lead plume over the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant region with an added opinion caption ("MAGA had warned of Iran setting off a dirty bomb..."). The linked article (Iowa Public Radio, Tom Barton, 2026-11-21) confirms, citing The New York Times, that the Army hired MuniRem Environmental in March to chemically neutralize nearly five tons of lead azide at the plant in Middletown and cancelled two months later, and that the plan uses sand barriers about two stories high plus water mist. The article adds context the post leaves out: the EPA and Army said the lead azide had recrystallized and that moving the 68 drums or even opening them could trigger an explosion, the Army acknowledged chemical treatment would avoid a lead plume, and a federal appeals court has temporarily put the EPA's emergency permit on hold. This is part of the trending "lead plume" topic.
